subject: german
title: Stamp 3: Recycling and Climate Law
welcome_lead: Stamp Germany's recycling system and climate law.
meta_desc: A-Level German adventure on recycling, Pfand, and the 2019 Climate Protection Act.

concepts.def: Deposit on drinks containers; refunded on return, encouraging recycling.
Refillable vs single-use; refillable bottles take a different deposit.
Green Dot; symbol on packaging indicating contribution to the recycling system.
Climate Protection Act setting binding emission reduction targets per sector.
Constitutional Court 2021 ruling that the Climate Act inadequately protected future generations.
Waste separation; households sort packaging (Gelber Sack), paper, glass, organic, and residual waste.

walkthroughs.body_html: Refundable deposits on plastic bottles (25 cents), cans (25 cents), and beer bottles (8 cents) drive return rates near 99%. Reverse-vending machines (Pfandautomaten) accept containers in supermarkets.
The 2019 Climate Protection Act set binding sectoral targets through 2030. After the 2021 Constitutional Court ruling, the act was tightened: -65% emissions by 2030, climate neutrality by 2045.
Households separate Papier (blue), Verpackungen (yellow), Glas by colour, Biomull (brown), and Restmull (black/grey). Germany has one of the world's highest recycling rates.
